entries.rationale: The source asks for a numerical count of ordered pairs of subsets subject to a nonempty-intersection condition. A case partition by the possible intersection size could clarify the counting structure, but the decisive work is combinatorial and a visual is not necessary; any visual must not imply cardinality through schematic area.

Each statement is a direct check of element membership, membership in the empty set, a less-than condition, or the cardinality of a two-element set under a≠b. No spatial or region fact is needed, and a visual would only duplicate the definitions.

Equality of the two explicitly listed two-element sets is resolved by matching the distinct elements −1 and 2, after which a+b is immediate. A Venn or other diagram adds no decisive mathematical fact.

The source gives a four-element set and asks only for its number of subsets, which is the direct 2^4 enumeration. A visual would duplicate a trivial counting rule rather than clarify a logical or spatial relation.

The cardinality identity reduces to A∩B=∅ and therefore A⊆B^c; the option that A∪B=B is not forced. A two-set Venn can make the disjointness and complement-inclusion relation explicit, but the same conclusion is fully recoverable from set algebra, so the visual is optional rather than required.
